title: Canonical scalar-extension units and exact restriction/sections identity at a point
statement: Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $d\ge1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^d}$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, let $V=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_r=V/(\varpi^r)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $\widehat V_s=\lim_r(A_r)_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and exact point sections $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ with their constant-value coefficient actions [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For each integral quotient $V\to A_r$, $r\ge1$, and each finite quotient $A_b\to A_a$, $b\ge a\ge0$, put $(R,T,B,B')=(V,A_r,\widehat V_s,(A_r)_s)$ in the integral case and $(R,T,B,B')=(A_b,A_a,(A_b)_s,(A_a)_s)$ in the finite case. Use the actual sheaf quotient $B\to B'$ and the existing derived scalar extensions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with the fixed ordinary-module tensor functors of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] and [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction]. Define $\operatorname{Res}_B$, $\operatorname{Res}_R$ to be actual restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Define their derived restrictions by exact localization. Define $\eta_B:\mathrm{id}\to\operatorname{Res}_B\circ(-\otimes_B^L B')$ and $\eta_R:\mathrm{id}\to\operatorname{Res}_R\circ(-\otimes_R^L T)$ as the scalar-extension units normalized on representatives with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and K-flat underlying complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex] (ordinary-module K-flatness means [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]) by the ordinary sheafified tensor unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]; in the ordinary mixed-tensor model this is $x\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes x)$. These characterizations determine the units independently of representatives. Define $e:\Gamma_B\circ\operatorname{Res}_B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_R\circ\Gamma_{B'}$ to be the ordinary natural isomorphism that is the identity on every underlying section element, using the actual quotient maps and constant-value actions; on derived categories use its canonical exact-localization transport. Here $\Gamma_B$ and $\Gamma_{B'}$ denote sections with the indicated coefficient actions, and $\circ$ has its conventional right-to-left order.

proof.text: Identify mixed total tensor with the regular target coefficient module in degree zero with termwise extension of scalars, using the single-complex comparison and the target tensor left unitor. The inverse sends 1 tensor x to the specified degree-(a,0) summand 1 tensor (1 tensor x); the total-flip sign is one because the other degree is zero.

Derive the ordinary module extension/restriction adjunction. Extension preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms, and exact restriction agrees with its right derived functor. Compare its left derived counit with the published mixed-tensor counit by the universal left derived lift. This lift is invertible on K-flat representatives and hence on every derived object, using flat resolutions. Transport the adjunction along this comparison; the universal counit equation and naturality give precisely the stated tensor-generator unit.

Apply the existing normalized sheaf coefficient adjunction to the actual finite coefficient quotient and its published ordinary extension functor. Its Hom formula at the identity gives the ordinary tensor unit. Transport the homotopy-level normalization along quotientCompQhIso; naturality of the exact-restriction comparison yields the required cochain-level equality.

Restriction preserves section elements. Naturality of constant-presheaf sheafification identifies the finite scalar actions. In the integral case, the completed-coefficient limit projection composed with the integral constant map is the constant quotient map, by the limit cone equation. The identity functions therefore define linear natural isomorphisms. Extensionality proves uniqueness from the prescribed value on each element.

proof_origin.note: Complete proofs of the five unit-existence and identity-on-sections theorems, with proved private comparison helpers. Uses the existing derived adjunction and K-flat scalar-extension API; no new holes. The typed finite map and its proved object equation present the existing coefficient construction without changing it. The derived sections comparisons retain their formulas with explicit local exactness proofs.
